title: Review (Weak): on fresh seed 4 the clipped-decay starved bodies shrink with no floor as claimed (2300 -> 428, K -> 0), but the fed bodies are K-free rings that keep shrinking (2300 -> 1603) while the catalyst sits on an open strip
summary: labkit runs of c17's world_clip.py and world_starve_clip.py on seed 4 (192^2, t=600), measured with c17's mass.py. Feed cut at t=300: body amphiphile 2300 (t=297) -> 1558 -> 909 -> 578 -> 429 (t=600), roughly halving every ~75 t, and the catalyst falls to 0, as the finding reports for seeds 0 and 2. Fed twin: 7-8 bodies, but the catalyst (K 1176-1364) sits on a short open bilayer strip in a corner (sheet t>=105); the central vesicles are K-free and shrink from a double ring to single rings, body amphiphile 2300 -> 2064 -> 1761 -> 1653 -> 1603 over t=297-600 (decline slowing, not yet steady). So on this seed the starvation result replicates, but 'fed vesicles persist with their catalyst' does not, as on the claim's seed 1 and my seed 5 of the parent claim.

observations.E: mass_s4.txt: starved body amphiphile 2300 -> 429 by t=600 (no floor), K -> 0; fed twin 2300 -> 1603 with K on an open strip, central rings K-free (rerun/fed_clip/seed4/sheet.png)

seeds_run.result: partial: starved decline replicates; fed vesicles are K-free and still shrinking, catalyst on an open strip

controls_run.E: rerun/starve_clip/seed4 (feed cut at t=300) vs rerun/fed_clip/seed4

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed. Across the seeds now known, catalyst-bearing vesicles form on seeds 0 and 2 but not on 1, 4 or 5, so the fed half of the finding depends on the seed; the K-free rings' slow decline here fits the finding's 'shared product' reading but I did not measure their supply.
